arguments.reasoning: Identify the shell that ran sudo useradd

steps.text: The ubuntu user tried useradd without sudo and failed, then succeeded with sudo—this fits the malicious attack simulation scenario. I'll submit with the host and ubuntu identity info, noting the new account entity isn't resolvable since we lack its id.

submission.reasoning: An interactive login shell (-bash, proc-10a8d311ba) running as user ubuntu on sysmonlinux-tcontreras-attack-range-643 first ran 'useradd atomic_user1' without privileges at 12:23:05 (proc-6e4a996727), which did not work. Four seconds later it ran 'sudo useradd atomic_user1' (proc-a347303d82), and sudo started useradd as root (proc-09d46fb4c7). That root process wrote and deleted account database files. pam_tally2 then reset the lockout counter for the new account (proc-53971473cc). This matches Atomic Red Team T1548.003 (sudo abuse) and local account creation (T1136.001): an unauthorized local account was created by escalating through sudo. To do: remove atomic_user1, rotate the ubuntu account's credentials and review its sudo rights, isolate the host, and check that /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow and /etc/group are back to their original state. The investigation did not return an entity for the new account itself, so it is not listed as an artifact.
